record.paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of almost periodic functions
record.context_brief: Converse characterization by ℓ^r Fourier coefficients
record.original_question: Let 1<r<2 and let x be an element of APr(R, C) with Fourier series ∑_{k=1}^∞ a_k e^{iλ_k t}. The paper notes that every such element has coefficient sequence (a_k) in ℓ^r, i.e. ∑_{k=1}^∞ |a_k|^r < ∞. Is the converse true: does every trigonometric series with coefficient sequence in ℓ^r determine an element of APr(R, C)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a real number $r$ with $1<r<2$. Consider trigonometric polynomials on $\mathbb{R}$ of the form $P(t)=\sum_{k=1}^{n} a_k e^{i\lambda_k t}$ with $a_k\in\mathbb{C}$ and $\lambda_k\in\mathbb{R}$, and define the seminorm
$$\|P\|_r=\Big(\sum_{k=1}^{n}|a_k|^{r}\Big)^{1/r}.$$
Let $\mathrm{AP}_r(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C})$ denote the completion of the space of such trigonometric polynomials with respect to $\|\cdot\|_r$. Each element $x\in\mathrm{AP}_r(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C})$ has an associated Fourier series $\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} a_k e^{i\lambda_k t}$ (with distinct real exponents $\lambda_k$), and one has $\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|a_k|^{r}<\infty$, i.e. $(a_k)\in\ell^r$.

Question: Is the converse true? That is, given any sequence of distinct real numbers $(\lambda_k)_{k\ge 1}$ and any sequence $(a_k)_{k\ge 1}\in\ell^r$, does the formal trigonometric series $\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} a_k e^{i\lambda_k t}$ determine (as the limit of its partial sums in $\|\cdot\|_r$) an element of $\mathrm{AP}_r(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C})$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the theory of almost periodic functions and asks for a Hausdorff–Young-type converse for the spaces AP_r with 1<r<2. A web search did not surface any subsequent paper establishing or refuting the converse, and standard references on almost periodic functions discuss only the direct (Hausdorff–Young) inclusion. The status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Fourier Analysis of Almost Periodic Functions (Springer)
status_evidence.snippet: Treatment of Fourier series of almost periodic functions, including the Hausdorff–Young inclusion but no converse for intermediate exponents.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references state only the direct inclusion of coefficients into ℓ^r without a converse for AP_r.

status_evidence.title: Almost Periodic Functions — C. Corduneanu
status_evidence.snippet: Monograph on almost periodic functions discussing AP_r spaces and their Fourier coefficients.
status_evidence.claim: The AP_r spaces and the ℓ^r property of their Fourier coefficients are introduced, but the converse characterization is left as a question.
